- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and prices are falling, model often underestimates the drop; adjust downward by 3–7% to match true decline.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overshoots in the following period; cap forecast at 10–15% below peak.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-period, model often fails to adjust; apply a “mean reversion” correction: subtract 1–3% of prior forecast if sentiment drops below 0.50.
- For 30-day forecasts, model consistently underestimates the “bottom” of the price cycle; add 1–3% to forecast if sentiment is neutral or bearish.
- If sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and price is volatile, model tends to over-smooth; increase forecast variance by 1–2% to reflect sentiment uncertainty.
